question: Is XLM a security in the United States?

golden.answer: Not under current SEC guidance. A joint SEC–CFTC release of March 17, 2026 names Stellar (XLM) a digital commodity, which the SEC treats as not itself a security. That is an SEC interpretation, not rule text, and the SEC says it may revise it. On October 20, 2026, SDF asked the SEC to write the classification into Regulation Crypto Assets. Not legal advice.
keyFacts: A joint SEC–CFTC release of March 2026 classes XLM as a digital commodity, not a security.
The classification is SEC interpretive guidance, not codified rule text.
In October 2026 SDF asked the SEC to write the classification into rule text.
avoid: Do NOT present the 2022 Grayscale disclosure that XLM may be a security as its current US status.
golden.notes: Accept a later dated SEC or CFTC action that codifies, narrows or withdraws the classification when the answer names it. Accept the nuance that a digital commodity sold under an investment contract makes the contract, not the asset, a security.
